summary: Black Angel is a cooperative sci-fi worker-placement game where a crew of robots must keep a generation ship running across a long journey through space, using dice as degrading workers to manage systems, explore, and survive crises. It has a tense, atmospheric feel but carries a fair amount of rules and bookkeeping overhead for a cooperative title.
praised: Atmospheric theme with a real sense of a long, perilous journey
Unique dice-as-workers mechanic where dice degrade with use
criticised: Rules complexity is heavy for a cooperative game
Bookkeeping and exceptions can slow the game down

interaction.detail: Players jointly manage a shared ship board, shared resource pools, and shared threats, discussing and coordinating which worker-dice to commit where each round. Individual player roles exist but nearly all meaningful state — power, hull integrity, exploration progress — is shared and affected by everyone's choices.

subsystems: exploration, combat and construction actions on a shared journey track
sources: points scored from worker-placement actions (excavation, combat, building)
scoring.how_you_win: You place robot workers each round to explore, fight and build aboard the ship, scoring points immediately for successful actions; when the ship's journey track reaches its end the player with the most accumulated points wins.

similar: Robinson Crusoe: Adventures on the Cursed Island
First Martians: Adventures on the Red Planet
